articles.title: Physicists propose new quantum device to measure how Earth twists space-time
articles.author: Larissa G. Capella

paras.en: Scientists have proposed a new tabletop device to detect the subtle way Earth's daily spin on its axis twists the space-time around it — an effect predicted by Einstein's general relativity.

If built, the sensor could measure the quantum effect known as frame dragging with the same precision as the best satellite experiments, but in minutes instead of years, the researchers proposed in a new study.

The research, published Sept. 17 in the journal Physical Review Letters, aimed to address a classic mismatch in physics. Picture a ring of clocks bolted to a spinning merry-go-round. You synchronize each clock with its neighbor around the ring. Then, you compare the last clock with the first. They don't match.

"It is impossible to synchronize that collection of clocks when you're in a rotating frame," Kai-Isaak Ellers, a physics graduate student at the University of California, Berkeley (UC Berkeley) and first author of the study, told Live Science.

Einstein's theory of general relativity predicts that a massive, spinning object drags the fabric of space-time along with it, just like a spoon twirling in honey. The effect is clearly visible around supermassive objects, like the Milky Way's central black hole. But around Earth, the effect is very faint.

So far, scientists have measured Earth's frame dragging only from orbit. They tracked how the twisting of space-time slowly shifts spinning gyroscopes or the paths of satellites. In 2011, NASA's Gravity Probe B satellite, which carried four gyroscopes, confirmed Einstein's prediction with a margin of error of about 18%. Satellites tracked with lasers have since done even better. In July, researchers reported in the journal Nature that the LARES-2 satellite had shrunk that margin of error to just 0.2%.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: However, that took about three years of laser tracking. Researchers also had to account for the fact that Earth bulges at the equator and its mass is spread unevenly, which gives the planet’s gravity small irregularities that tug on satellites far more strongly than frame dragging does. To subtract those tugs, the team relied on detailed maps of Earth's gravity made by other satellites.

Measuring frame dragging more precisely is a way to stress-test general relativity. Several alternative theories of gravity predict a slightly different amount of twisting, and a lab-based measurement would also be free of the modeling assumptions that satellite experiments depend on, Ellers said.

The new device is a loop of superfluid helium-4 — helium chilled until it flows without friction and behaves like a single, giant quantum object. The loop is interrupted by a thin barrier riddled with tiny holes, called a Josephson junction. Superfluid helium can slip through the holes, but ordinary liquid helium cannot.
"That's where the quantum behavior comes from," said K. Birgitta Whaley, a quantum physicist at UC Berkeley and a co-author of the study.

As Earth spins and drags space-time, it nudges the quantum state of the helium flowing through the junction. That nudge shifts the frequency at which the helium sloshes back and forth in the loop, which the researchers could detect.

Superfluid devices, many of them built at UC Berkeley, have detected Earth's rotation since the late 1990s. But the helium-4 versions built around a Josephson junction, like the new design, have worked within about a hundredth of a degree of 2.17 K (minus 455.76 Fahrenheit, or minus 270.98 Celsius), the temperature at which helium-4 becomes a superfluid. At that temperature, a lingering fraction of "normal" helium mixed in with the superfluid adds noise.

Instead, the team calculated how the device would behave at a few thousandths of a degree above absolute zero. Below 0.7 K, the noise changed character, and the team found it drops sharply as the helium gets colder. One key finding in the new paper is the result of the team's thermal noise analysis, which showed how sensitive these devices could be at millikelvin temperatures, Elles said.

The catch is the barrier. Earlier helium-4 devices used holes about 90 nanometers wide. Working at these frigid temperatures demands much smaller holes, about 1 nanometer across — roughly the size of a helium atom. Keith Schwab, a physicist at Caltech and co-author of the study, and his collaborators are developing such materials, but they haven't been built into a working sensor yet.

If they can be, the researchers calculate that the device could measure frame dragging to 0.2% precision in about 35 minutes. If its vibrating membrane were made from the lowest-loss crystals, such as quartz or sapphire, that could drop to about one second, they said.
- In a first, physicists spot elusive 'free-range' atoms — confirming a century-old theory about quantum mechanics
- 'Crystals' of space-time could be the origins of certain rare black holes, theoretical study hints
- 'Time was speeding up, slowing down, or even stopping': Physicist demonstrates a key theory of time by building a 'mini-universe' in his lab
"This seems to be a very serendipitous discovery that at millikelvin, we can get this high sensitivity," Whaley told Live Science.
The signal corresponds to a time difference of about 10-35 seconds between helium flowing one way around the loop and the other — the same mismatch as the clocks on the metaphorical merry-go-round.

"The interesting thing about it is just how small it is," Whaley said. "It's not so far off from the Planck time," about 10-44 seconds, the shortest slice of time before the known laws of physics are expected to break down. This experiment is still a billion times too large to reach that limit, Whaley said. But future helium experiments could help explore whether time flows smoothly, like a ramp, or ticks forward in tiny, indivisible jumps, like the frames of a movie.

articles.title: Neolithic Cannibalism Wasn't an Act of Desperation. Almost 1,000 Skeletal Fragments From Caves in Southern Spain Show How Eating Human Flesh Was a Continual Practice

paras.en: For generations, human cannibalism in prehistoric Europe was viewed as a desperate response to starvation. Now, a forensic re-examination of three prehistoric cave sites in southern Spain reveals that people ate human remains as a ritual for millennia, including after violent clashes or as a standard funeral rite.

Researchers analyzed 967 skeletal fragments representing at least 60 individuals recovered from the caves of Malalmuerzo, Carigüela and Majolicas in the province of Granada. Using high-resolution microscopy, machine learning and radiocarbon dating, the team discovered that these grisly feasts were not confined to a single crisis, such as war or starvation. Instead, they unfolded in “context-dependent episodes” between roughly 5300 B.C.E. and 3760 B.C.E., according to a recent study published in the Journal of Archaeological Science.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: The bone assemblages were first excavated in the 1970s under the direction of Miguel C. Botella, a forensic anthropologist at the University of Granada. Fifty years later, Botella joined a multi-disciplinary team to subject the historical collection to modern forensic analysis.

“Returning to these materials with new tools has allowed us to address questions that were impossible to answer at the time,” lead author Palmira Saladié, an archaeologist at the Catalan Institute of Human Paleoecology and Social Evolution, explains in a statement.

By scrutinizing butchery traces, impact fractures and tooth marks under the microscope, the researchers distinguished between injuries inflicted on fresh bone around the time of death and natural degradation that took place years later. The skeletons bore unmistakable hallmarks of systematic butchery: defleshing cut marks, bones split open to harvest marrow, crushed crania to extract brain tissue and bones rendered translucent from boiling.

Despite common processing methods, each cave documented a distinct social reality behind the cannibalistic practices. Remains from Malalmuerzo Cave—which coincidentally translates to “Bad Lunch,” Botella tells Joshua Rapp Learn of the New York Times—likely date to an episode of communal violence around 5000 B.C.E. There, 77 percent of the 714 recovered fragments displayed fractures, Historia National Geographic’s Juan Pedro Chuet-Missé reported in September.

“At Malalmuerzo … our analyses indicate the presence of remains from all age groups, which would suggest a violent event in which all or almost all the individuals in a group were killed and subsequently consumed,” co-author Antonio Rodríguez-Hidalgo, an archaeologist at the Institute of Archaeology of Mérida, says in the statement.

Children’s remains from Malalmuerzo also bore human tooth marks indicative of “very intensive consumption,” co-author Ana Solari, an anthropologist at Argentina’s National Scientific and Technical Research Council, tells the Times.

In contrast, Carigüela Cave revealed recurrent visits across more than a millennium, from approximately 5470 B.C.E. to 3650 B.C.E. Among its 43 human remains, researchers identified two “skull cups”—craniums from an adult and a child that had been carefully broken and retouched along the edges to function as drinking vessels, a mortuary pattern seen at other European sites like El Mirador in Spain and Herxheim in Germany.

At Majolicas Cave, occupied between 3950 B.C.E. and 3760 B.C.E., cannibalism was decoupled from evidence of interpersonal violence. The remains, primarily belonging to adults between 18 and 45, were found coated in reddish pigments identified as cinnabar, a rare mineral associated with death rites.

Instead of an act of desperation, eating the dead appears to have been an accepted funerary tradition. While other contemporary European communities practiced internment, burial in open-air graves or, starting in fifth millennium B.C.E., burial in communal megalithic tombs, the dwellers of these southern Spanish caves may have bid farewell to their dead by consuming them.

The absence of any alternative funerary practice such as burial or cremation in the cave further strengthens this explanation. “The great majority of them, they didn’t kill them,” Botella tells the Times. “They just died; and after they died, they ate them.” He speculates that these communities may have consumed deceased relatives or friends to keep them connected to their lives, drawing a parallel to mortuary cannibalism historically recorded in parts of South America.

Silvia Bello, a palaeoanthropologist and an expert in human cannibalism at the Natural History Museum in London who was not involved in the research, tells the Times that the consumption most likely occurred between members of the same group, though marks of blunt-force trauma on skulls from Malalmuerzo still point to occasional episodes of lethal violence.

“For decades, prehistoric cannibalism has tended to be interpreted as a single type of behavior,” Rodríguez-Hidalgo adds in the statement. “Our work shows that … similar archaeological evidence may conceal very different social realities.”

articles.title: While Cleaning Out Her Aunt's Manhattan Apartment, a Woman Found a Long-Lost Georgia O'Keeffe Painting Buried Beneath Fur Coats in the Closet

paras.en: Most people’s closets are littered with life’s spare change—broken umbrellas, unpaired socks and discarded scraps of elementary school artwork. But while cleaning out her elderly aunt’s New York City apartment, one woman made a staggering discovery in the closet. Underneath a pile of fur coats sat a Georgia O’Keeffe landscape painting that had been tucked away for four decades.
When she made the discovery, Betsy, who asked to be referred to by only her middle name, was shocked. “I thought, ‘Wow. That’s pretty wild,’” she tells the New York Post’s Natalie O’Neill.

The 1930 painting, Near Abiquiu, New Mexico I, is thought to be the first in a series of three paintings depicting Lobo Peak in northern New Mexico. (The second is at the Metropolitan Museum of Art and the third is in a private collection.) It will hit the auction block as part of Christie’s 20th Century Evening Sale on November 17. Estimates place the piece’s value between $3 million and $5 million.

“To uncover a seminal work—representative of this 20th century master’s deep personal engagement with the landscape, a pillar of her career, which is exquisitely rendered and well preserved—is a once-in-a-lifetime moment and absolutely thrilling,” Tylee Abbott, head of American Art at Christie’s New York, says in a statement.
The artwork features warm earth tones and soft, rippling hills, an early iteration of the abstracted New Mexico landscapes she would paint throughout her career.

“O’Keeffe goes to New Mexico in 1929, and this picture is from 1930, so it’s the ground floor of her inspiration at that time,” Abbott tells CBS News’ Noelle Lilley. “And she is very vocal about, in her writings and things, about how impactful it was on her. I think you get that in this picture.”

Betsy’s aunt, a career Foreign Service worker and world-ranked bridge master, acquired Near Abiquiu in 1963. It was a graduation gift from her parents, purchased directly from O’Keeffe’s New York dealer for $3,800, roughly $42,000 today.

She displayed the modernist piece in her New York apartment for decades. But one day in the mid-1980s, in the middle of a bridge game, she noticed a guest eyeing the painting a little too closely. Out of an abundance of caution, she hid the piece in her entry closet, carefully enclosing the 10-by-24-inch painting in its original box and tucking it behind rows of fur coats.
Did you know? A controversial characterization
- Many critics “projected sexual meanings onto the alluring, inward-curving petals” of O’Keeffe’s enlarged flower paintings, Smithsonian magazine’s Jennie Rothenberg Gritz writes.

- O’Keeffe disputed those characterizations: “When you took time to really notice my flower, you hung all your associations with flowers on my flower and you write about my flower as if I think and see what you think and see of the flower—and I don’t.”
“I think she was fully aware of its value,” Betsy explains to the Post. “She recognized that it was an expression of her financial position. … She disliked drawing attention to herself.”

That meant keeping Near Abiquiu away from all curious eyes, even family members. Betsy had no knowledge of the treasure hidden in her aunt’s closet until 2022, when the pair were preparing the apartment for the arrival home health aides. “That’s when she mentioned, ‘Oh, by the way, there’s a Georgia O’Keeffe in the hall closet,” she tells the Post.
But it wasn’t until a few weeks ago, when Betsy returned to help her since-deceased aunt prepare for hospice, that she finally laid eyes on the artwork itself.

Until its rediscovery, the painting was known to the art world from a sole 1931 photograph, taken by O’Keeffe’s husband, Alfred Stieglitz. Christie’s was able to identify the work using the photograph and O’Keeffe’s distinctive, looping signature in a star-shaped design on the back.

“We certainly use just a visual analysis of looking at the painting, looking at the styles, how the brush strokes may match, how other O’Keeffes appear that we’ve known that we’ve sold,” Abbott tells CBS News. “But also, O’Keeffe is very well-documented with a [catalogue raisonné] that published all [her] known works ... This work, of course, appears in the addendum of that as ... ‘unlocated.’”
After decades languishing as “unlocated,” concealed among piles of fur, the painting is now on public view at Christie’s New York through November 17, ahead of its auction.

articles.title: A Rare Surviving Letter From Martha Washington Sheds Light on Her Young Daughter's Struggle With Epilepsy

paras.en: More than 260 years ago, Martha Washington wrote to a friend with encouraging news about her young daughter’s health. Now, that letter has found a new home at the Library of Congress, offering a rare glimpse into the family’s private life.
Martha penned the note on September 29, 1760. Writing to Margaret Bolan Green, she provided an update on her four-year-old daughter “Patsy.”
“I have the pleasure to tell you my dear little girl is much better,” she wrote. “She has lost her fitts & fevours bout and seems to be getting well very fast.”

The Library of Congress purchased the letter for $47,500 in June during a Heritage Auctions sale, with funding from the James Madison Council’s Edwin L. Cox Legacy Trust, a permanent endowment that helps the library acquire materials. The library already had 11 of Martha’s letters, but this is the first that bears her handwriting.

“Very few of Martha Washington’s letters survive, as she appears to have destroyed most of her own private correspondence,” Elizabeth Novara, the American women’s history specialist for the library’s Manuscript Division, writes in a blog post. “Even brief documentation of her relationships with family and friends, as may be found in this letter, is important to understanding women’s lives during this time period.”

“Patsy”—whose full name was Martha Parke Custis—was one of the four children Martha had with her first husband, Daniel Parke Custis. The two had been married for just seven years when Custis died from a sudden illness in July 1757, at the age of 45. Two years later, at age 27, the widowed Martha married George Washington. Together, they raised the two surviving children from Martha’s first marriage, Patsy and John “Jacky” Parke Custis. (The other two, Daniel Parke Custis and Frances Parke Custis, died while their father was still alive.).
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Historians believe that William Costin, a prominent member of Washington, D.C.’s free Black community, was likely Martha Washington’s grandson—the child of her son from her first marriage, Jacky, and an enslaved woman.

Martha wrote the letter after George Washington had served as commander of the Virginia Regiment during the French and Indian War but before he had become the nation’s first president. Historians now suspect that Patsy’s “fitts & fevours” were symptoms of epilepsy, a neurological disorder caused by abnormal bursts of electrical activity in the brain. But, at the time, doctors didn’t understand her affliction.

“There’s no doubt that [Patsy] had epilepsy,” Kevin Butterfield, acting chief of the library’s manuscript division, tells the Washington Post’s Michael E. Ruane. “In her preteen and teen years it really accelerated.”

The Washingtons consulted numerous doctors and tried a variety of remedies to stop Patsy’s seizures, including an iron ring worn on one finger, bloodletting, trips to mineral springs and treatments with mercury and ether. They also gave her cinchona bark, commonly used to treat malarial fevers, and bitters, a remedy for stomach ailments.

But Patsy’s epilepsy only worsened. In the summer of 1770, when Patsy was 14, her stepfather kept track of her epileptic fits. His log revealed that she had seizures on 26 out of 86 days, sometimes suffering two per day.

In the end, it was a seizure that killed Patsy. She died at age 17 on June 19, 1773, at Mount Vernon “without uttering a Word, a groan or scarce a Sigh,” George Washington wrote the next day. The death of the “Sweet Innocent Girl” was a “sudden, and unexpected blow” that “almost reduced my poor Wife to the lowest ebb of Misery,” he added.

The Library of Congress also recently acquired a letter written by First Lady Mary Todd Lincoln. She penned the note to Caroline R. Wright, the wife of the former governor of Indiana, on February 15, 1865, two months before her husband was assassinated.

In the letter, she mentions a “beautiful wreath of hair,” which scholars suspect is a reference to the “Hairy Eagle,” an intricate sculpture created from the locks of several politicians and their wives, including the Lincolns. Wright commissioned the piece to be used as a fundraiser for sick and wounded Civil War soldiers.

The letter also references a recent White House dinner and renovations to the Executive Mansion that would prevent the Lincolns from hosting visitors in early March. Mary Todd Lincoln suggests Wright might stay at Willard’s Hotel, now the site of the Willard InterContinental, during a visit that historians think might coincide with Abraham Lincoln’s second presidential inauguration on March 4, 1865.

Together, the two newly acquired letters help the Library of Congress “tell fascinating stories that we simply couldn’t tell before,” Butterfield says in a statement. “What is already the world’s richest and most expansive collection of materials related to American history is constantly growing—sometimes one letter at a time.”

articles.title: The AO3 Shutdown Is Pitting Fanfic Readers Against Authors
articles.author: Michaela Makusha

paras.en: Avery has been writing fan fiction for about six years, now mainly focused on the gay hockey romance Heated Rivalry. Until last month, it all lived in one place—Archive of Our Own. Then, on October 29 the fan fiction behemoth went dark due to a “security incident.” Within days, Avery was alarmed to find her works on mirror sites she hadn’t posted them to.
“To me it’s a security risk,” Avery, who did not want her real name used due to fears of backlash on social media, tells WIRED via DM. “One bad actor could put malware in that drive.”

She emailed the sites—Squidgeworld and AO3.Life—and the stories were removed, though she’ll never know if she has found every copy online. (AO3.Life has since been taken down, and Walter Hopgood, president of Squidge.org, which hosts Squidgeworld, told WIRED it removes works that are posted without an author’s permission.)
Avery’s problem is one shared with many fanfic authors since the team behind AO3 announced the site will remain offline for up to four weeks.

Hosting more than 18.8 million fan works across hundreds of thousands of fandoms, AO3 is among the most visited websites in the world. When it went down, some fans started freaking out over the “AO3 apocalypse.” Within days, readers who had saved stories on their own device placed them onto shared libraries on Google Drives. But finding alternatives has caused friction in the community, as some authors are unhappy with the way their works are being distributed without their permission, breaking fanfic norms and exacerbating fears about AI scraping.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: One of the many drives to pop up was the Archive Salvation Google Drive project, a collective of fan fiction downloaded from AO3. It faced criticism after launching, though a spokesperson tells WIRED it offered ways for authors to ask for their work to be removed. But it’s since been hacked and is no longer accessible, according to a November 3 statement on a moderator’s TikTok, though the group behind it is still sharing fanfics in a closed Discord server.

“We continue to acknowledge the controversies of such drives but also want to acknowledge the joy this has brought readers and the authors who submitted their fics to us,” the statement said, adding, “our drive was controversial and very public, so the hacker is most likely someone who stands against drives like this in general.”
Avery doesn’t mind her work circulating in private drives or being asked for copies of their work for fans to read—her concern is with her work being uploaded to giant drive libraries.

But she says AO3’s breakdown has revealed entitlement among some readers, who’ve messaged her demanding to know where her fics are now available. “I just can’t wait for AO3 to go back up so that people can go back to normal,” she says. “It’s left a sour taste in my mouth.”

“Writers hating their readers this much will kill fandoms actually,” one user wrote on X in response to an artist expressing frustration about people who “don’t contribute anything to the fandom” weighing in on how work is shared. Another X user accused the same artist of being “self-righteous” and “entitled.”

Avery says some readers seem to feel authors’ feelings “are secondary to the readers.” “It feels like AO3 going down made so many people so crazy that they couldn’t get their fix, and I think the authors are most outspoken because it’s our work.”

Riley, a writer with over 90,000 followers across X and Instagram, ran afoul of some fellow authors when they shared a Google doc cataloging some of the drives compiling fanfic on November 2. Some people claimed it was a privacy violation and could put AO3 users at risk of doxing. “It’s about basic respect,” one user wrote, while others demanded their fics be removed from the list.
Riley, who did not want their real name used for fear of receiving more backlash, made their X account private soon after.
“I did not anticipate the potential harmful effects of me compiling the document of stories, which is why I deleted it,” they tell WIRED.

Meanwhile, Ellipsus, a collaborative writing platform with an anti-AI stance that was founded in 2022, has seen a boom in interest since AO3 went down. Allegra Rosenberg, an Ellipsus employee and writer, says that new sign-ups are up more than 500 percent since the outage began and views of its public reader links—the ways in which authors can share work—have increased heavily.

What Ellipsus offers is control. Authors can control who can see their work and how they can interact with it. They can turn on comments, and readers can leave kudos (called “props” on Ellipsus), as well as custom fonts and themes. Rosenberg says the company noticed that many of the users were fan fiction writers and adjusted features for them before the outage, for example, a button that exports work directly to AO3.
”We know that people want a space to not only write but share new writing, in a way that feels safe for them,” says Rosenberg.

Another reason the outage has felt so fraught is that the world of fan fiction has broken containment, becoming mainstream in part due to shows like Heated Rivalry and the adaptation of former fan fictions such as Alchemised by SenLinYu, which was originally published on AO3, into bona fide novels.

“It’s the Tik-tokification of fanfic,” Avery says.“Everyone wants a snippet and a graphic and a one shot, and they can share it on Twitter, and then suddenly a thing I wrote years ago goes viral. Fan fiction never used to go viral.”

Rosenberg, who is writing a book on fandom, thinks that so much of the backlash comes from a mismatch between how big the community actually is and how small it still feels to many. The giant drives and libraries drew outrage due to their scale and a fear from many fans that their stories could be taken down. That fear has a real history within fandom spaces.

“In the ’90s and 2000s, there were cease-and-desist notices and takedown controversies on Fanfiction.net and LiveJournal that led to AO3’s founding,” Rosenberg explains. “So there is this shared history and memory within fandom culture as a whole when it comes to fan fiction.”

The demand for fan fiction does not come only from people active in fandom circles. It also comes from people who are seen as casual fans—those who are not as invested in the wider fandom. Fan fiction operates on norms where people ask permission, and there is a tolerance for a certain level of informal sharing. The AO3 outage has tested these norms and has exposed the lack of practical protection an author has once their work is posted. Readers are doing what they have always done—sharing work that they love. However, the burden of this sharing is uneven, as authors fear losing track of their own work.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: “I think this whole AO3 going down thing has reminded people that the internet is forever for better or for worse,” Avery says. “Long after I die, if we still have the internet, my fics will float about even without AO3.”

articles.title: A Startup Wants to Fight AI Bioweapons With AI
articles.author: Emily Mullin

paras.en: Frontier AI labs have warned that their technology could help develop dangerous bioweapons.
paras.zh: 前沿人工智能实验室已警告称，他们的技术可能被用于开发危险的生物武器。

paras.en: Now, a startup says it has developed a defense. On Wednesday, Radical Numerics announced that it has developed a new edge model called Omnii Defense that is designed to flag natural and AI-engineered pathogens using a laptop and a USB gene sequencer. It can also run without an internet connection, allowing researchers in the field with spotty connections to use it. Though many scientists say AI-made bioweapons are a low-likelihood threat, Radical Numerics hopes its technology will help researchers and public health officials identify emerging biological threats.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Eric Nguyen, cofounder and CEO of Radical Numerics, says he sees a coming arms race in biodefense similar to what’s playing out in cybersecurity, where threat actors and security defenders are leveraging AI in an attempt to gain an edge.
paras.zh: Radical Numerics的联合创始人兼首席执行官Eric Nguyen表示，他认为生物防御领域即将迎来一场军备竞赛，类似于网络安全领域正在上演的竞赛，其中威胁行为者和安全捍卫者都在利用人工智能来试图取得优势。

paras.en: “We felt that the biosecurity space was far behind on the defense side,” he says.
paras.zh: “我们觉得，在防御方面，生物安全领域远远落后。”他说。

paras.en: Nguyen and his cofounders were part of the research team behind Evo and Evo-2, open-source DNA foundation models they worked on during their doctoral research at Stanford University. They founded Radical Numerics in 2025.
paras.zh: 阮先生和他的联合创始人是Evo和Evo-2背后的研究团队成员，Evo和Evo-2是他们在斯坦福大学攻读博士学位期间研究的开源DNA基础模型。他们于 2025 年创立了 Radical Numerics。

paras.en: The San Francisco–based company recently made waves after rolling out Omnii, a new genome language model built on different types of biological information beyond DNA, including RNA, proteins, and epigenetic signals. In October, Radical announced that it used Omnii to create custom bacteriophages, viruses that infect and kill specific bacteria, targeting a drug-resistant strain of E. coli. Its cocktail was used to treat a sick patient, with special permission from the Food and Drug Administration.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Another AI biotech startup, Tabula Bioscience, was also involved in that research, but Radical didn’t disclose the partnership in its announcement last month. The omission led Harvard geneticist George Church, who was an adviser to both companies, to resign from his role at Radical last week.
paras.zh: 另一家人工智能生物技术初创公司Tabula Bioscience也参与了该项研究，但Radical在上个月的公告中并未披露这一合作关系。这一疏漏导致曾担任两家公司顾问的哈佛大学遗传学家乔治·丘奇（George Church）上周辞去了他在Radical的职务。

paras.en: Omnii Defense, the company’s latest tool, makes multiple predictions about a sequence, including the odds of it being pathogenic or AI-generated and what taxonomic group it most closely resembles. The model assigns a genome a “threat score” between zero and one that combines the likelihood of unnaturalness with functional predictions. The higher the score, the higher the threat.
paras.zh: Omnii Defense是该公司的最新工具，它对一个序列做出多项预测，包括该序列具有致病性或由人工智能生成的可能性，以及它最接近哪个分类群。该模型为基因组赋予一个介于0和1之间的“威胁评分”，该评分将非自然性的可能性与功能预测相结合。分数越高，威胁越大。

paras.en: Earlier biodefense tools, such as the federally funded Finding Engineering-Linked Indicators, or Felix, can compare genetic sequences of interest against libraries of known organisms, essentially searching for cataloged matches. That can be helpful in a scenario where a bad actor has made a few tweaks to an existing pathogen. But they aren’t designed to make predictions in the way that Omnii is.
paras.zh: 早期的生物防御工具，如联邦政府资助的“寻找工程关联指标”（Felix），可以将目标基因序列与已知生物体库进行比较，本质上是在寻找已编目的匹配项。在不法分子对现有病原体进行了一些微调的情况下，这可能很有帮助。但它们的设计目的并非像Omnii那样进行预测。

paras.en: The benefit of AI models is that they can learn patterns in sequences associated with biological function instead of relying on exact sequence matches. That could allow them to recognize similarities between sequences even when their genetic spelling has changed. Christine Parthemore, Radical Numerics’ head of biodefense, says Omnii is a “step change.”

In one experiment, the company removed Bundibugyo virus—which is currently driving an Ebola outbreak in East Africa—from the training data, first at the species level and then its whole genus. “It was as if Omnii was operating in 1976,” Parthemore says, referring to the year Ebola was discovered. With just the species removed, the model still detected that 33 percent of the Bundibugyo sequences pushed to it were something pathogenic. Even with the whole genus removed, it flagged 22 percent of the viral sequences. Non-AI tools gave essentially no indication of potential risk, she says.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: “We absolutely need to be vigilant about what AI is enabling, and if we can use technology to compete with it and hopefully get ahead of any kind of nefarious actors, that seems sensible,” says Bronwyn MacInnis, director of pathogen surveillance in the Infectious Disease and Microbiome program at the Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard.
However, MacInnis cautions that detecting a signal is still a big leap from determining whether a pathogen has real consequence or whether a threat was engineered.

Access to Omnii Defense is currently limited to vetted external testers. Radical Numerics says it is working with national laboratories, government agencies, and other independent evaluators to assess the model’s performance.

paras.en: My pick for the best budget Wi-Fi router dips down to this price fairly often, but it’s a great deal for a Wi-Fi 7 router with four antennas, a 2.5-Gbps WAN, a 2.5-Gbps LAN, and three gigabit LAN ports. It’s only dual-band (2.4 GHz and 5 GHz), so there’s no 6-GHz option, and performance is limited, but for a small home with modest demands, this is a tough price to beat.
paras.zh: 我选出的性价比最高的 Wi-Fi 路由器经常会降到这个价格，但对于一款配备四根天线、2.5 Gbps WAN、2.5 Gbps LAN 和三个千兆 LAN 端口的 Wi-Fi 7 路由器来说，这个价格已经非常划算了。它仅支持双频（2.4 GHz 和 5 GHz），因此没有 6 GHz 选项，性能也有限，但对于需求适中的小户型家庭来说，这个价格很难被超越。

paras.en: A good laptop docking station lets you convert your laptop into a desktop for a comfier experience when you’re working from home, and this compact beauty from Belkin is one of our top picks. GaN technology (gallium nitride semiconductors, a faster, more compact alternative to silicon) lets Belkin pack more ports than you can shake a USB-C cable at, including 96-watt power delivery, three 4K display ports, a gigabit Ethernet port, and more. This deal equals the lowest price we’ve seen.
paras.zh: 一款出色的笔记本电脑扩展坞可以让您将笔记本电脑变成台式机，在家办公时获得更舒适的体验，而这款来自Belkin的精致小巧产品就是我们的首选之一。得益于氮化镓技术（氮化镓半导体，一种比硅更快、更紧凑的替代品），Belkin 能够集成比您能想到的还要多的端口，包括 96 瓦的功率输出、三个 4K 显示端口、一个千兆以太网端口等。此优惠价格是我们见过的最低价。

paras.en: This security camera records video at up to 2K at 30 frames per second, offers a 150-degree field of view, and connects directly to your Wi-Fi network. The Tapo app can detect motion (person, pet, vehicle) and enables you to set activity zones and privacy zones. The two-way audio is okay, and there’s a built-in alarm function. You can also slip a microSD card in for local recording. It lacks HDR, but it still earns a spot in our best outdoor security cameras guide. It has bounced between $90 and $65 for the last year, but it’s now down to $60.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: It may not be one of the best video doorbells you can buy, but at this sale price, Blink’s latest wired doorbell is the cheapest option worth considering. It delivers reasonably good 2K footage and passable two-way audio, though it’s definitely less responsive than some other options on the market. If you want person detection and cloud storage, you’ll also need to spring for the subscription (from $3 a month). The battery version is also on sale at $39 ($41 off).
paras.zh: 它可能不是您能买到的最好的可视门铃，但以这个售价来看，Blink的最新有线门铃是最值得考虑的廉价选择。它提供相当不错的2K画质和尚可的双向音频，但响应速度肯定不如市场上的一些其他产品。如果您想要使用人体检测和云存储功能，还需要购买订阅服务（每月3美元起）。电池版也在促销，售价 39 美元（立减 41 美元）。

paras.en: Permanent outdoor lights are a great way to avoid having to get up the ladder every holiday season. They offer simple white lighting, different colors, and also holiday-themed lighting effects. Eufy’s lights aren’t the brightest, but they hold up well against the competition and support Matter, so you can tie them into any smart home ecosystem. All lengths are on sale, but the 200-foot string has the best discount and is at its lowest price ever.
paras.zh: 使用永久性户外灯具，就不必在每个节日季都爬上梯子。它们提供简单的白色照明、不同的颜色，以及节日主题的灯光效果。Eufy的灯具并非最亮，但它们在竞争中表现出色，并且支持Matter，因此您可以将它们接入任何智能家居生态系统。所有长度的灯串均有优惠，但 200 英尺的灯串折扣最大，价格创历史新低。

paras.en: If you like to run an organized household, the best digital wall calendars are sure to appeal. You can use them to sync your digital calendars, create lists of chores, and plan your family meals. The Everblog HomeCal is our pick for folks who can’t stomach another subscription. It also works like a digital photo frame if you upload your snaps, and you can log into apps like Netflix and Spotify on it. This is the lowest we’ve seen it drop so far. Clip the coupon for an extra $50 off.
paras.zh: 如果您希望井井有条地打理家务，那么最好的数字挂历一定会让您心动。您可以使用它们同步数字日历、创建家务清单并规划家庭用餐。对于那些不想再订阅其他服务的人来说，Everblog HomeCal是我们推荐的选择。如果您上传照片，它还可以像数字相框一样使用，您还可以在上面登录Netflix和Spotify等应用程序。这是我们迄今为止看到的最低价格。使用优惠券可额外优惠 50 美元。

paras.en: Learning about the wildlife in your garden can be a lot of fun, and the best smart bird feeders are an ideal way to see which feathered friends are in the area. The thoughtfully designed Kiwibit Bird Feeder 2 has a removable 1.5-liter dual-hopper seed reservoir, is easy to clean, and boasts a solar roof to keep the camera charged up. It snaps 8-megapixel photos, captures 4K video, and includes a nifty AI bird-identification feature. We’ve seen it on sale before, but never this low.
paras.zh: 了解花园里的野生动物可能很有趣，而最好的智能喂鸟器是观察该地区有哪些羽毛朋友的理想方式。精心设计的 Kiwibit Bird Feeder 2 配备可拆卸的 1.5 升双料斗式鸟食储存罐，易于清洁，并配备太阳能顶盖，可为摄像头持续充电。它能拍摄 800 万像素的照片，录制 4K 视频，并配备了巧妙的人工智能鸟类识别功能。我们之前见过它打折，但从来没有这么低过。

paras.en: If you have a challenging lawn, this may be the best robot mower for you. It can navigate rough terrain, steep slopes, and tree cover with its combination of GPS, lidar, and AI vision, cutting grass evenly and accurately. This version can cover 0.75 acres, and is at the lowest price I've ever seen it.
paras.zh: 如果您有棘手的草坪，这款机器人割草机可能是您的最佳选择。它结合了GPS、激光雷达和AI视觉技术，能够在崎岖地形、陡坡和树荫下导航，均匀、准确地修剪草坪。此版本可覆盖0.75英亩，价格是我见过的最低价。

paras.en: This affordable espresso machine is even more affordable than usual right now. It's got a shiny chrome finish, with buttons for steam and single or double shots, plus a pressure gauge, a 15-bar pump, an effective steam wand, and fast heating. We've seen it dip lower ($120), but it's still a bargain at $150.
paras.zh: 这款价格实惠的意式浓缩咖啡机现在比平时更实惠。它采用闪亮的镀铬饰面，设有蒸汽按钮以及单份或双份浓缩咖啡按钮，还配备了压力表、15巴泵、高效蒸汽棒和快速加热功能。我们曾看到过更低的价格（120美元），但150美元仍然物超所值。

paras.en: This cordless vacuum boasts three cleaning modes, a HEPA filter, and a newly designed cleaner head. It can handle hard floors and soft carpet, with dual rotating conical brush bars that prevent tangled hair. It's our top pick of the more affordable Dyson vacuum cleaners, and it’s cheaper than we've ever seen it right now.
paras.zh: 这款无绳吸尘器具备三种清洁模式、HEPA滤芯和新设计的吸尘头。它配备双旋转锥形刷条，可防止毛发缠绕，适用于硬质地板和柔软地毯。这是我们精选的更实惠的戴森吸尘器，现在比我们见过的任何时候都便宜。

paras.en: With the ability to mop and vacuum your floors, map multiple floors, and self-clean, the Eufy Omni C28 is a decent option for most homes. This is the budget pick in our best robot vacuums guide. Despite the $800 MSRP, it often drops to $500, but it's even less than that right now, a better deal than usual.
paras.zh: Eufy Omni C28具备拖地和吸尘、多层楼层建图以及自清洁功能，是大多数家庭的理想之选。这是我们在最佳扫地机器人指南中的经济型之选。尽管建议零售价为 800 美元，但它通常会降至 500 美元，而现在甚至比这还要低，比平时更划算。

articles.title: 'Grey's Anatomy' spinoff casts first lead: Karla Souza

paras.en: Nov. 11 (UPI) -- Karla Souza has landed a lead role in the upcoming Grey's Anatomy spinoff series.
paras.zh: 11月11日（UPI）——卡拉·索萨（Karla Souza）将在即将上映的《实习医生格蕾》衍生剧中担任主角。

paras.en: The Wrap reported Wednesday that Souza, 40, will reunite with Grey's Anatomy and How to Get Away with Murder creator Shonda Rhimes on the untitled show.
paras.zh: 《The Wrap》周三报道称，40岁的苏扎将在这部暂未命名的剧中与《实习医生格蕾》（Grey's Anatomy）和《逍遥法外》（How to Get Away with Murder）的创作者珊达·莱梅斯（Shonda Rhimes）再度合作。

paras.en: Souza played Laurel Castillo on How to Get Away with Murder, and is also known for portraying Marina on Home Economics.
paras.zh: 索萨在《逍遥法外》（How to Get Away with Murder）中饰演劳雷尔·卡斯蒂略（Laurel Castillo），还因在《家庭经济学》（Home Economics）中饰演玛丽娜（Marina）而知名。

paras.en: Deadline confirmed Souza's casting and said the actress will play Carolina "Lina" Hall, "a haunted and cynical doctor" who runs a rural medical center in West Texas.
paras.zh: Deadline证实了索萨的选角，并表示这位女演员将饰演卡罗莱娜·“莉娜”·霍尔（Carolina “Lina” Hall），一位“心事重重且愤世嫉俗的医生”，她在西德克萨斯州经营一家乡村医疗中心。

paras.en: The spinoff is created by Rhimes and Meg Marinis, who also serves as showrunner.
paras.zh: 这部衍生剧由莱姆斯和梅格·马里尼斯（Meg Marinis）创作，后者还担任该剧的制片人。

paras.en: Originally announced at ABC in May, the series was initially launch during the 2026-2027 broadcast season but was delayed a year after failing to receive a California TV tax credit, according to Variety.
paras.zh: 据《综艺》报道，该剧最初于5月在ABC宣布，原定于2026-2027播出季首播，但由于未能获得加利福尼亚州电视税收抵免，播出时间被推迟了一年。

paras.en: The original Grey's Anatomy, starring Ellen Pompeo, Chandra Wilson and James Pickens Jr., is in its 23rd season on ABC. The show inspired the previous spinoffs Private Practice and Station 19.
paras.zh: 由艾伦·旁派、钱德拉·威尔逊和詹姆斯·皮肯斯· जूनियर主演的原版《实习医生格蕾》正在ABC电视台播出第23季。这部剧启发了此前的衍生剧《私人诊所》和《火线警魂》。

articles.title: Russian ambassador to the U.S. Alexander Darchiev dies suddenly, officials say

paras.en: Nov. 11 (UPI) -- Russia's ambassador to the United States, Alexander Darchiev, has died suddenly at age 66, the Russian Foreign Ministry said Wednesday.
paras.zh: 11月11日（UPI）——俄罗斯外交部周三表示，俄罗斯驻美国大使亚历山大·达尔切夫（Alexander Darchiev）突然去世，享年66岁。

paras.en: The ministry did not disclose the cause of Darchiev's death. In a statement, it called him an "an outstanding diplomat, experienced leader, kind colleague and mentor," and a "professional of the highest order and a brilliant expert on American affairs."
paras.zh: 该部未透露达尔契耶夫的死因。该部在一份声明中称他是“杰出的外交官、经验丰富的领导者、友善的同事和导师”，以及“最高级别的专业人士和出色的美国事务专家”。

paras.en: Darchiev had served as Russia's ambassador to the United States since March 2025. He entered diplomatic service in 1992 and served in many roles, including as Russia's ambassador to Canada from 2014 to 2021, the Russian Embassy said. He was a former leader of the Russian Foreign Ministry's North Atlantic Department, based in Washington, D.C.
paras.zh: 达尔奇耶夫自2025年3月起担任俄罗斯驻美国大使。俄罗斯大使馆表示，他于1992年进入外交部门工作，曾担任多个职务，包括2014年至2021年担任俄罗斯驻加拿大大使。他曾是俄罗斯外交部北大西洋事务司的负责人，该司设在华盛顿特区。

paras.en: Darchiev followed Anatoly Antonov as ambassador to the United States. He was a protégé of Russian President Vladimir Putin's foreign policy adviser Yury Ushakov, The Moscow Times reported.
paras.zh: 达尔契耶夫接替阿纳托利·安东诺夫担任驻美国大使。据《莫斯科时报》报道，他是俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京的外交政策顾问尤里·乌沙科夫的门生。

paras.en: When Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022, Darchiev called it a "necessary measure," The Guardian reported. In December 2025, when the Senate Appropriations Subcommittee on State, Foreign Operations and Related Programs held a hearing on Russian abductions of Ukrainian children, the late Sen. Lindsey Graham, R-.S.C., invited Darchiev to the hearing, but the ambassador did not attend.
paras.zh: 据《卫报》报道，当俄罗斯在2022年入侵乌克兰时，达尔契耶夫称之为“必要措施”。2025年12月，当参议院拨款委员会的国务院、对外行动及相关方案小组委员会就俄罗斯绑架乌克兰儿童一事举行听证会时，已故的南卡罗来纳州共和党参议员林赛·格雷厄姆邀请达尔契耶夫出席听证会，但这位大使并未出席。

paras.en: The World Bank reports the average life expectancy for a man in Russia is about 68 years.
paras.zh: 世界银行报告称，俄罗斯男性的平均预期寿命约为68岁。

articles.title: Paraguan evangelical pastor faces investigation in Ueno case

paras.en: ASUNCION, Paraguay, Nov. 11 (UPI) -- Paraguayan prosecutors said Wednesday they plan to investigate evangelical pastor Joshua Abreu, a former securities regulator and Ueno brokerage director, as part of their probe into the bank's collapse.
paras.zh: 巴拉圭亚松森11月11日电（合众国际社）——巴拉圭检察官周三表示，他们计划调查前证券监管机构兼上野经纪公司董事、福音派牧师约书亚·阿布鲁（Joshua Abreu），作为对该银行倒闭调查的一部分。

paras.en: Prosecutor Francisco Cabrera said officials will examine operations between Ueno Bank and Ueno Casa de Bolsa, a brokerage firm, and Abreu's role as a director, ABC Color reported.
paras.zh: 据 ABC Color 报道，检察官弗朗西斯科·卡布雷拉 (Francisco Cabrera) 表示，官员们将审查上野银行 (Ueno Bank) 和经纪公司上野 Casa de Bolsa 之间的业务，以及阿布鲁 (Abreu)​​ 担任董事的角色。

paras.en: The inquiry would extend beyond the allegedly irregular loans and overdrafts examined so far, Cabrera said.
paras.zh: 卡布雷拉表示，调查范围将超出迄今为止所审查的涉嫌违规贷款和透支的范围。

paras.en: ABC also reported that staff at the brokerage allegedly tried to destroy documents related to former President Santiago Peña shortly before a raid by prosecutors and police.
paras.zh: 美国广播公司还报道称，在检察官和警方进行突袭之前不久，该经纪公司的工作人员据称试图销毁与前总统圣地亚哥·佩纳有关的文件。

paras.en: Abreu is a pastor at Centro Familiar de Adoración, an evangelical church with congregations across Paraguay. Its online directory lists 74 churches.
paras.zh: 阿布雷乌是Centro Familiar de Adoración的牧师，该福音派教会的会众遍布巴拉圭各地。该教会的在线名录列出了74座教堂。

paras.en: He requested temporary leave from his ministerial duties, according to the same ABC report. Church leaders urged members to avoid speculation about the decision. The church had police protection Sunday amid threats of demonstrations, the newspaper reported.
paras.zh: 据同一篇ABC新闻报道，他请求暂时卸任牧师职务。教会领袖敦促教众避免对该决定进行猜测。该报报道称，由于存在示威威胁，该教会周日得到了警方的保护。

paras.en: Abreu is also the son-in-law of José Alberto Alderete, Peña's former political adviser, according to ABC.
paras.zh: 据ABC报道，阿布雷乌还是佩尼亚的前政治顾问何塞·阿尔贝托·阿尔德雷特的乘龙快婿。

paras.en: In a Sept. 13 sermon on generosity, Abreu discussed his interest in finance and recalled his grandmother buying him U.S. Treasury bonds as birthday gifts.
paras.zh: 在9月13日关于慷慨的布道中，阿布雷乌谈到了他对金融的兴趣，并回忆起他的祖母曾为他购买美国国债作为生日礼物。

paras.en: The brokerage's website lists him as a principal director. The bank's financial statements also list him as an alternate director as of March 31.
paras.zh: 该经纪公司的网站将他列为首席董事。该银行的财务报表也将其列为截至3月31日的候补董事。

paras.en: He previously headed Paraguay's securities regulator, resigning in January 2025.
paras.zh: 他曾担任巴拉圭证券监管机构的负责人，并于2025年1月辞职。

paras.en: The Central Bank announced resolution proceedings against Ueno Bank on Nov. 3, saying its solvency ratio had fallen below half the required minimum. The securities supervisor has also suspended the brokerage's operations, except to complete previously agreed transactions.
paras.zh: 日本央行于11月3日宣布对上野银行启动破产处置程序，称该行的资本充足率已降至法定最低标准的二分之一以下。证券监管机构还暂停了该券商的业务，但允许其完成此前已达成的交易。

articles.title: BigXthaPlug Scores His First No. 1 Rap Album With ‘Better Over Time’
articles.author: Trevor Anderson

paras.en: BigXthaPlug scores his first No. 1 on Billboard’s Top Rap Albums chart as Better Over Time debuts atop the list dated Nov. 14. The set, released on BigXthaPlug/United Masters, starts with 35,000 equivalent album units earned in the United States for the tracking week of Oct. 29-Nov. 5, according to Luminate.
paras.zh: BigXthaPlug 在 11 月 14 日首张专辑《Better Over Time》中首次登上公告牌最佳说唱专辑榜第一名。这张专辑在 BigXthaPlug/United Masters 上发行，在 10 月 29 日至 11 月的跟踪周内在美国获得了 35,000 个同等专辑单位。 5、根据Luminate。

paras.en: Better Over Time’s first-week figure breaks down into 29,000 units from streaming activity (representing 29.1 million official on-demand streams of the album’s songs), traditional album sales contributing 6,000 units and a negligible number of track-equivalent sales. (One unit equals the following levels of consumption: one album sale, 10 individual tracks sold from an album, or 1,000 paid/subscription tier or 2,500 ad-supported tier official on-demand audio and video streams for a song on the album.)
paras.zh: 《Better Over Time》首周销售量分为 29,000 份来自流媒体活动（代表专辑歌曲的 2910 万份官方点播流），传统专辑销量贡献了 6,000 份，而曲目当量销量则微不足道。 （一个单位等于以下消费水平：一张专辑销售、一张专辑中销售的 10 首单独曲目，或专辑中一首歌曲的 1,000 个付费/订阅层或 2,500 个广告支持层的官方点播音频和视频流。）

paras.en: Thanks to the new album, the Dallas-based rapper born Xavier Landum achieves his first No. 1 on Top Rap Albums with his fourth entry. He first reached the ranking in 2024 with Take Care, which debuted and peaked at No. 3, while 2025’s I Hope Your Happy secured him the runner-up rank. Earlier this year, 600 Entertainment: NWA — a collaborative project with Ro$ama and other artists — reached No. 25.
paras.zh: 凭借这张新专辑，出生于达拉斯的说唱歌手泽维尔·兰杜姆 (Xavier Landum) 凭借他的第四张专辑首次登上了热门说唱专辑榜第一名。他于 2024 年凭借《保重》首次登上排行榜，首张专辑便登上了第 3 名的巅峰，而 2025 年的《祝你幸福》让他获得了亚军。今年早些时候，与 Ro$ama 和其他艺术家合作的项目 600 Entertainment: NWA 达到了第 25 位。

paras.en: In addition to its chart-topping rap opening, Better Over Time launches at No. 2 on the Top R&B/Hip-Hop Albums chart, a new career peak, and at No. 7 on the all-genre Billboard 200, matching I Hope You’re Happy for the rapper’s best showing.
paras.zh: 除了在说唱专辑排行榜上名列前茅之外，《Better Over Time》在 R&B/Hip-Hop 专辑排行榜上排名第二，创下了职业生涯的新高峰，并在所有类型的 Billboard 200 排行榜上排名第七，与说唱歌手 I Hope You're Happy 的最佳表现不相上下。

paras.en: Largely due to its streaming performance, Better Over Time lands 10 tracks on the 50-position Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs chart. Current single “Burn,” featuring Ava Max, ranks highest, pushing 27-14 as both the week’s Sales Gainer and Streaming Gainer for the largest improvements in both metrics. Previous release “Lite,” featuring Belly Gang Kushington, reenters at No. 27 to capture a new peak in its third week on the chart.
paras.zh: 《Better Over Time》在 50 名热门 R&B/Hip-Hop 歌曲排行榜上占据了 10 首曲目，这在很大程度上归功于其流媒体表现。目前由 Ava Max 主演的单曲《Burn》排名最高，以 27 比 14 的成绩成为本周的销量增长者和流媒体增长者，在这两个指标上都有最大的进步。 Belly Gang Kushington 主演的上一张专辑《Lite》重新进入第 27 名，在排行榜第三周创下新高。

paras.en: Here’s a list of BigXthaPlug’s placements on this week’s Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs chart, all debuts excluding “Burn” and “Lite.”
paras.zh: 以下是 BigXthaPlug 在本周热门 R&B/Hip-Hop 歌曲排行榜上的排名列表，所有首张歌曲均不包括“Burn”和“Lite”。

paras.en: - No. 27, “Lite,” feat. Belly Gang Kushington
paras.zh: - 第 27 号，“Lite”壮举。肚皮帮库欣顿

paras.en: - No. 48, “Believe,” feat. Babyface Ray & Lil Yachty
paras.zh: - 第 48 号，“相信”壮举。娃娃脸雷和莉尔·游艇

paras.en: The eight new arrivals bring BigXthaPlug to 31 career entries on Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs. “Burn” becomes his third-highest charting title, after his and Lil Wayne’s collab “Hip-Hop,” featuring Jay Jones (No. 8 in 2025) and “MMHMM” (No. 11, 2024).
paras.zh: 这八位新人将 BigXthaPlug 的热门 R&B/Hip-Hop 歌曲收录到了 31 首歌曲中。 《Burn》成为他的第三高排行榜冠军，仅次于他和 Lil Wayne 与 Jay Jones 合作的《Hip-Hop》（2025 年排名第 8）和《MMHMM》（2024 年排名第 11）。

articles.title: Beyoncé Gets ‘Goosebumps’ From RAYE, Sienna Spiro & Olivia Dean: ‘I Just Burst With Pride When I See Them’
articles.author: Hannah Dailey

paras.en: Beyoncé thinks RAYE is that girl — and so are Sienna Spiro and Olivia Dean.
paras.zh: 碧昂斯 (Beyoncé) 认为 RAYE 就是那个女孩，西耶娜·斯皮罗 (Sienna Spiro) 和奥利维亚·迪恩 (Olivia Dean) 也是如此。

paras.en: Queen Bey praised the three rising stars, two of whom she has personal connections to, in an interview with i-D published Wednesday (Nov. 11). While on the topic of launching her Cecred hair-care brand in the U.K., she said she loves the country’s music scene before naming a few examples.
paras.zh: Queen Bey 在周三（11 月 11 日）发表的 i-D 采访中赞扬了这三位冉冉升起的新星，其中两位与她有私人关系。在谈到在英国推出她的 Cecred 护发品牌时，她表示自己很喜欢这个国家的音乐场景，然后举了几个例子。

paras.en: “I’ve watched Sienna Spiro grow up from a beautiful young girl to an extraordinarily talented young woman,” Bey told the publication. “I’ve known her family well for quite some time. I heard her sing when she was a kid discovering her voice, and I can’t articulate the pride she brings me. What a God-given talent!”
paras.zh: “我看着西耶娜·斯皮罗从一个美丽的年轻女孩成长为一个非常有才华的年轻女性，”贝告诉该出版物。 “我很了解她的家人很长一段时间了。当她还是个孩子的时候，我发现了自己的声音，我听过她唱歌，我无法表达她给我带来的自豪。这是上帝赐予的天赋！”

paras.en: The 35-time Grammy winner is linked to the Spiro family by way of Sienna’s father, jeweler Glenn Spiro, who’s been curating and designing pieces for Bey for years. In 2018, she made headlines for donating an eye-catching butterfly ring gifted to her by Jay-Z and designed by Mr. Spiro to the Victoria and Albert Museum in London.
paras.zh: 这位 35 届格莱美奖得主与 Spiro 家族的渊源是 Sienna 的父亲、珠宝商 Glenn Spiro，后者多年来一直为 Bey 策划和设计珠宝。 2018 年，她因将 Jay-Z 送给她的、由 Spiro 先生设计的引人注目的蝴蝶戒指捐赠给伦敦维多利亚和阿尔伯特博物馆而成为头条新闻。

paras.en: Also in the interview, the Destiny’s Child alum shouted out RAYE, who worked for years as a songwriter penning hits for stars such as Bey before breaking out in 2023 with independent smash “Escapism.” “I’m also so proud of RAYE, who wrote some of the songs on The Gift,” Bey said. “She has had such an anointing. You hear the vulnerability and wisdom in her voice.”
paras.zh: 同样在采访中，这位《天命真女》的演员还点赞了 RAYE，他多年来一直担任词曲作者，为 Bey 等明星创作热门歌曲，然后在 2023 年凭借独立热门单曲《Escapism》崭露头角。 “我也为 RAYE 感到骄傲，他为 The Gift 创作了一些歌曲，”Bey 说。 “她受到了这样的恩膏。你可以从她的声音中听到脆弱和智慧。”

paras.en: “I also love and respect Olivia Dean,” the haircare mogul added. “These beautiful women are all kind, have grace and write and produce their own music. It gives me goosebumps. I just burst with pride when I see them.”
paras.zh: “我也爱并尊重奥利维亚·迪恩，”这位护发大亨补充道。 “这些美丽的女性都很善良、优雅，她们自己创作音乐。这让我起鸡皮疙瘩。当我看到她们时，我感到无比自豪。”

paras.en: Like Spiro and RAYE, Dean has experienced a major rise in the past couple of years. She took home best new artist at the Grammys in 2026, an award for which RAYE was nominated the year prior, and for which Spiro is highly anticipated to be up for in 2027.
paras.zh: 与 Spiro 和 RAYE 一样，Dean 在过去几年中经历了巨大的进步。她于 2026 年在格莱美颁奖典礼上获得了最佳新人奖，RAYE 在前一年获得了该奖项的提名，而 Spiro 也有望在 2027 年获得该奖项。

paras.en: As the three Brits have dominated in 2025 and 2026, Bey has kept a low profile musically. She hasn’t dropped an album since 2024’s two-week Billboard 200-topper Cowboy Carter, though fans are holding out hope that her long-awaited Act III is coming any day now.
paras.zh: 由于三位英国人在 2025 年和 2026 年占据主导地位，贝伊在音乐上一直保持低调。自 2024 年连续两周荣登公告牌 200 强专辑《Cowboy Carter》以来，她就没有再发行过任何一张专辑，尽管歌迷们仍对她期待已久的第三幕即将到来抱有希望。

articles.title: Primary Wave and Kobalt CEOs Discuss Their Billion-Dollar Partnership — And Why ‘You’ll See a Lot More’ Consolidation in Music
articles.author: Kristin Robinson

paras.en: In February, Billboard broke the news that Primary Wave was nearing a historic deal to acquire Kobalt, arguably the world’s largest independent frontline publisher. Together, it was estimated that the newly combined company would be worth a staggering $7 billion in assets.
paras.zh: 今年 2 月，Billboard 爆料称 Primary Wave 即将达成收购 Kobalt 的历史性交易，Kobalt 可以说是全球最大的独立一线发行商。据估计，新合并后的公司的资产总价值将达到惊人的 70 亿美元。

paras.en: By July, the deal finally closed. But given that no one from the two companies had yet spoken to the press, major questions remained about how this new arrangement would operate in practice. All that was disclosed at the time was that Kobalt would operate independently of Primary Wave, one of the largest owners of iconic music catalogs in the industry, with a roster spanning from Whitney Houston to Stevie Nicks to Bob Marley to Prince.
paras.zh: 到了七月，交易终于完成。但鉴于两家公司中尚未有任何人向媒体发表讲话，因此这一新安排将如何在实践中运作仍存在重大疑问。当时所披露的只是 Kobalt 将独立于 Primary Wave 运营，Primary Wave 是业内最大的标志性音乐目录所有者之一，其成员包括惠特尼·休斯顿 (Whitney Houston)、史蒂夫·尼克斯 (Stevie Nicks)、鲍勃·马利 (Bob Marley) 和 Prince。

paras.en: But would Primary Wave move all of its catalogs to Kobalt? Did the deal include assets from Kobalt’s $700m catalog fund with Morgan Stanley? And how do Kobalt’s other verticals fit into the picture? The independent publisher is also home to AMRA, a global digital rights collection service that aims to speed up royalty collection and cut out middlemen outside of the U.S., and Kosign, its digital-first publishing service for middle-class songwriters who are not ready to sign a traditional deal.
paras.zh: 但是 Primary Wave 会将其所有目录转移到 Kobalt 吗？该交易是否包括 Kobalt 与摩根士丹利合作的 7 亿美元目录基金的资产？ Kobalt 的其他垂直领域如何融入其中？这家独立出版商还是 AMRA 和 Kosign 的所在地，AMRA 是一项全球数字版权收集服务，旨在加快版税收取速度并减少美国以外的中间商，而 Kosign 则是为尚未准备好签署传统协议的中产阶级歌曲作者提供数字优先出版服务。

paras.en: News of the acquisition also came at a time of seismic change in the music industry. Universal Music Group’s Virgin division was finalizing its acquisition of Downtown Music Holdings and BMG was moving toward its purchase of Concord, reshaping the state of independent music in a matter of months.
paras.zh: 此次收购的消息传出之际正值音乐行业发生巨变之际。环球音乐集团 (Universal Music Group) 的维珍 (Virgin) 部门即将完成对 Downtown Music Holdings 的收购，而 BMG 则正在着手收购 Concord，从而在几个月内重塑了独立音乐的现状。

paras.en: To explain Primary Wave and Kobalt’s new deal for the first time and why all of this consolidation is happening now, Primary Wave founder/CEO Larry Mestel and Kobalt CEO Laurent Hubert joined Billboard’s music business podcast, On the Record.
paras.zh: 为了首次解释 Primary Wave 和 Kobalt 的新交易以及为什么现在发生所有这些整合，Primary Wave 创始人/首席执行官 Larry Mestel 和 Kobalt 首席执行官 Laurent Hubert 加入了 Billboard 的音乐商业播客 On the Record。

paras.en: To watch this episode of Billboard On the Record, check out the YouTube video below or click here for more viewing and listening options. An edited and condensed excerpt of the conversation can also be found below.
paras.zh: 要观看 Billboard On the Record 的这一集，请查看下面的 YouTube 视频或单击此处获取更多观看和收听选项。下面还提供了经过编辑和浓缩的对话摘录。

paras.en: When did you guys start discussing this deal?
paras.zh: 你们什么时候开始讨论这笔交易的？

paras.en: Hubert: I think the beginning of the conversation was some time in the summer of 2025. I think the first conversation was not a direct conversation with me but with another party at a particular dinner.
paras.zh: 休伯特：我认为谈话是在 2025 年夏天的某个时候开始的。我认为第一次谈话不是与我直接对话，而是在一次特定的晚宴上与另一方进行的对话。

paras.en: Mestel: I remember that dinner, and Primary Wave has historically been administration-agnostic. We’re into the value creation business, not the administration business. So we’ve always used Kobalt or Universal or some other administrators instead of creating our own internal administration platform.
paras.zh: 梅斯特尔：我记得那次晚餐，Primary Wave 历来与政府无关。我们从事价值创造业务，而不是管理业务。因此，我们一直使用 Kobalt 或 Universal 或其他一些管理员，而不是创建我们自己的内部管理平台。

paras.en: The dinner Laurent was speaking about was a dinner that I believe Goldman Sachs had organized. I remember at that dinner, Jenny Kim, who is head of music now at Goldman, came up to me and said, “Have you considered Kobalt as an acquisition and as a partner?” And I said, “Well, we’re administration-agnostic, but I’ve known Laurent forever. Culturally, I think we’re very similar companies.” She said, “Well, you’re going to consider it because I’m bringing you the deal.” And so I said, “Great, let’s consider it.”
paras.zh: 劳伦特所说的晚宴我相信是高盛组织的。我记得在那次晚宴上，现任高盛音乐主管的珍妮·金 (Jenny Kim) 走过来对我说：“你是否考虑过收购 Kobalt 并成为合作伙伴？”我说，“好吧，我们与政府无关，但我永远认识洛朗。在文化上，我认为我们是非常相似的公司。”她说：“好吧，你会考虑一下，因为我正在为你带来这笔交易。”所以我说：“太好了，让我们考虑一下。”

paras.en: At the end of the day, it made a lot of sense for us because you could never have on your team too many great managers, and Laurent’s team are fantastic managers. We saw some jewels inside of Kobalt, not just the administration platform, which is really fantastic, but divisions like AMRA and Kosign, too.
paras.zh: 归根结底，这对我们来说很有意义，因为你的团队永远不会有太多优秀的经理，而洛朗的团队都是出色的经理。我们在 Kobalt 内部看到了一些瑰宝，不仅是非常棒的管理平台，还有像 AMRA 和 Kosign 这样的部门。

paras.en: Why not do administration in-house at Primary Wave?
paras.zh: 为什么不在 Primary Wave 内部进行管理？

paras.en: Mestel: For us, the focus has always been on marketing, on branding, on creating content, doing Broadway, doing movies, doing immersive experiences, creating cosmetic lines, you know, gaming, etc. So there’s a real core competency to that, and it’s very hard for other companies that are competitors to recreate what we recreate. To build an administration platform takes a significant amount of capital and takes a significant amount of effort. And we always viewed it as a commodity, where there were a lot of industry players that did administration, but not many — in fact, I can’t even name any — that does really great marketing and value creation. So we’ve always stayed away from the administration side of the business because we could always rent it at relatively insignificant cost.
paras.zh: 梅斯特：对我们来说，重点一直是营销、品牌、内容创作，做百老汇、做电影、做沉浸式体验、创造化妆品系列、你知道的、游戏等等。所以这是真正的核心能力，而其他竞争对手的公司很难复制我们所复制的东西。建设一个管理平台需要大量的资金和大量的精力。我们总是将其视为一种商品，有很多行业参与者进行管理，但没有多少——事实上，我什至不能说出任何人的名字——真正能进行出色的营销和价值创造。因此，我们始终远离业务的管理方面，因为我们总是可以以相对较低的成本租用它。

paras.en: You’ve said before that Kobalt is going to stand on its own, but you guys have complementary strengths. Where are the two companies going to work together?
paras.zh: 你们之前说过，Kobalt 将独立发展，但你们有互补的优势。两家公司将在哪些领域开展合作？

paras.en: Hubert: I have to credit Larry for the vision for the business because initially, when we first talked, I understood the interest, but I did not fully understand the vision. And then I think Larry explained that very clearly, saying, “Hey, we understand Kobalt. We understand what it means in the market and that it’s a destination today.” He says also he built a destination — which I think is very unique — and we create value differently. You know, for Primary Wave, it’s really about how do you create engagement on the properties that they acquired, and for us, it’s how do we unlock greater value from a collection perspective.
paras.zh: 休伯特：我必须归功于拉里对业务的愿景，因为最初，当我们第一次交谈时，我理解了兴趣，但我并没有完全理解愿景。然后我认为 Larry 解释得非常清楚，他说：“嘿，我们了解 Kobalt。我们了解它在市场上的意义，并且它是当今的目的地。”他还说他还建立了一个目的地——我认为这是非常独特的——我们以不同的方式创造价值。你知道，对于 Primary Wave 来说，真正重要的是如何让他们所收购的财产产生参与感，而对于我们来说，这就是我们如何从收藏的角度释放更大的价值。

paras.en: From that perspective, we saw a direct opportunity, and some of it will be that we will cross some functionality that we have, and we’ll compound those benefits without talking about merger or integration. That was also interesting for us from a management perspective because we felt we didn’t have to go through an education process about Kobalt. We don’t have to be disrupted day one. We could keep going and do what we do the best we can do.
paras.zh: 从这个角度来看，我们看到了一个直接的机会，其中一些机会是我们将交叉我们拥有的一些功能，并且我们将在不谈论合并或整合的情况下将这些好处复合起来。从管理角度来看，这对我们来说也很有趣，因为我们觉得我们不必经历有关 Kobalt 的教育过程。我们不必从第一天就受到干扰。我们可以继续前进，尽我们所能。

paras.en: Larry, you mentioned that there were some jewels within Kobalt that you were super interested in. You mentioned AMRA, and it’s interesting because I’ve heard similar phrasing back when Francisco Partners purchased Kobalt in 2022. They called AMRA an “unpolished gem.” So I’m curious why you think it’s a gem as well?
paras.zh: Larry，你提到 Kobalt 中有一些你非常感兴趣的珠宝。你提到了 AMRA，这很有趣，因为我在 2022 年 Francisco Partners 收购 Kobalt 时就听到过类似的说法。他们称 AMRA 是“未抛光的宝石”。所以我很好奇为什么你也认为它是宝石？

paras.en: Mestel: Those that aren’t using AMRA are going local. How long does it take for you to collect your money? Eight months, 12 months, 15 months. AMRA is going direct, and it’s very hard to recreate AMRA because of the history of AMRA and the licenses that they’ve put in place. So, it’s touching your money sooner, and there are less people with their hands in your pocket. It’s really that simple. I think the more people discover AMRA, the more people are going to want to use AMRA. We have $7.5 billion worth of assets now within Primary Wave. We’re going to be putting as much of our repertoire through AMRA as we possibly can.
paras.zh: Mestel：那些不使用 AMRA 的公司正在转向本地化。您需要多长时间才能收到钱？八个月、12个月、15个月。 AMRA 正在直接进行，由于 AMRA 的历史和他们所颁发的许可证，很难重新创建 AMRA。所以，你的钱能更快拿到手，把手插在你口袋里的人也更少了。真的就是这么简单。我认为越多的人发现 AMRA，就会有越多的人想要使用 AMRA。 Primary Wave 目前拥有价值 75 亿美元的资产。我们将尽可能多地通过 AMRA 提供我们的曲目。

paras.en: Larry, do you plan to switch all the Primary Wave catalogs over to do publishing admin through Kobalt now as well?
paras.zh: Larry，您现在是否打算将所有 Primary Wave 目录切换到通过 Kobalt 进行发布管理？

paras.en: Mestel: We have some great partners around the world, and I’ll name two: Kobalt and Universal. We give Universal quite a bit of our administration worldwide. They are an excellent administration organization. We have a great relationship with Jody [Gerson, CEO of UMPG] and Mark [Cimino, COO of UMPG] and David [Kokakis, chief counsel of UMPG] and the team there. Kobalt will be getting much more of Primary Wave repertoire than it has gotten in the past, but we won’t be taking anything away that we’ve given Universal, and we’ll continue to give Universal more work in the future because they’ve done a great job.
paras.zh: 梅斯特尔：我们在世界各地有一些很棒的合作伙伴，我举两个：Kobalt 和 Universal。我们在全球范围内向环球影业提供了相当多的管理权。他们是一个优秀的管理组织。我们与 Jody [Gerson，UMPG 首席执行官]、Mark [Cimino，UMPG 首席运营官] 和 David [Kokakis，UMPG 首席法律顾问] 以及那里的团队有着良好的关系。 Kobalt 将获得比过去更多的 Primary Wave 曲目，但我们不会拿走我们给予环球的任何东西，并且我们将在未来继续给予环球更多的工作，因为他们做得很好。

paras.en: I guess you also can’t just stop in the middle of an administration agreement with another company, like UMPG, just because you bought Kobalt this year.
paras.zh: 我想你也不能仅仅因为今年购买了 Kobalt，就停止与 UMPG 等另一家公司签订管理协议。

paras.en: Mestel: We have very short-term deals, but we’re not going to do that. The reason is that when you do short-term deals, you keep partners engaged. If you put up a long-term deal, maybe there’s less incentive. So I like to do month-to-month, quarter-to-quarter, year-to-year. I don’t like much more than year-to-year.
paras.zh: 梅斯特尔：我们有非常短期的交易，但我们不会这样做。原因是，当你进行短期交易时，你可以让合作伙伴保持参与。如果你签订的是长期协议，可能激励就会减少。所以我喜欢按月、按季度、按年进行。我不喜欢比年复一年更多的事情。

paras.en: We are very well capitalized, and the fact that we’re very well-capitalized means we don’t need advances because when you take advances, that means you lower your margin. I’d rather have a much higher margin, no advance.
paras.zh: 我们的资本非常充足，事实上我们的资本非常充足，这意味着我们不需要预付款，因为当你接受预付款时，就意味着你的利润会降低。我宁愿有更高的利润，也没有预付款。

paras.en: Luminate CEO Rob Jonas recently came on this podcast and revealed that now 150,000 songs are being uploaded to streaming services every day. With the sheer volume of music now, how has that changed your approach?
paras.zh: Luminate 首席执行官 Rob Jonas 最近在这个播客中透露，现在每天有 150,000 首歌曲上传到流媒体服务。现在音乐的数量如此之多，这对你的方法有何改变？

paras.en: Mestel: I think that’s much more relevant for Laurent than it is for me because we are in the icon and legend business. We’re buying only the greatest of the great.
paras.zh: 梅斯特尔：我认为这对劳伦特来说比对我更重要，因为我们从事的是偶像和传奇行业。我们只购买伟大中的最伟大的。

paras.en: Hubert: Frankly, in the past 10-15 years, the way we manage publishing has totally transformed. We went from an ownership to a consumption model. Obviously, we went from a few hundred income sources to literally thousands of income sources.
paras.zh: 休伯特：坦率地说，在过去的 10 到 15 年里，我们管理出版的方式已经完全改变了。我们从所有权模式转变为消费模式。显然，我们从几百个收入来源变成了数千个收入来源。

paras.en: We also have seen fragmentation of copyright. It’s not uncommon to see five, seven writers on a song, and you have fragmentation of consumption. So if you look at those factors, it has compounded volume in [many] ways, and the challenge with volume is you need to manage that with great velocity because we have to account every quarter. [Just] because you have more to manage [doesn’t mean] that you can delay your accounting period, obviously. Plus, you also have [more] challenges with accuracy. Our job as we build the infrastructure — it’s a continuous exercise — is, how do we manage this?
paras.zh: 我们还看到版权的碎片化。一首歌有五、七个作者的情况并不罕见，而且消费也存在碎片化。因此，如果你看看这些因素，它会以[许多]方式复合数量，而数量的挑战是你需要以极快的速度管理它，因为我们必须每个季度都进行核算。显然，[只是]因为您有更多需要管理[并不意味着]您可以推迟会计期间。另外，您在准确性方面还面临[更多]挑战。我们构建基础设施时的工作（这是一项持续的工作）是，我们如何管理它？

paras.en: I’ve often had a conversation with my CTO: How do we manage [Amazon Web Services] cost? All of it is in the cloud. You have volume growing at 30%-40% a year, and you have your cost of AWS growing at 10%-12% a year, and we have to manage the business. You have to find ways to, again, optimally manage that ecosystem without affecting velocity. It’s frankly a job of every day. It really is. It’s a natural tension in the business.
paras.zh: 我经常与我的 CTO 交谈：我们如何管理 [Amazon Web Services] 成本？所有这一切都在云端。业务量每年增长 30%-40%，AWS 成本每年增长 10%-12%，我们必须管理业务。同样，您必须找到在不影响速度的情况下优化管理该生态系统的方法。坦率地说，这是每天的工作。确实如此。这是业务中自然的紧张关系。

paras.en: So, are publishers spending more than ever to try to collect all these royalties all over the world?
paras.zh: 那么，出版商是否比以往任何时候都花费更多的钱来尝试在世界各地收取所有这些版税？

paras.en: Hubert: We are. The challenge is that the value of that micro license or micro transaction is so small that you have to do it cost-effectively; otherwise you’d be losing money [to collect it]. Technology is obviously a major aspect of what we do. AI is, of course, but it’s not only AI — it’s about building infrastructure that can handle the volume. It’s a challenge. This is a topic that we talk about almost every day.
paras.zh: 休伯特：我们是。挑战在于，微许可或微交易的价值是如此之小，以至于您必须经济高效地进行操作；否则你就会赔钱[去收集]。技术显然是我们工作的一个主要方面。当然，人工智能是，但它不仅仅是人工智能——它还涉及构建能够处理大量数据的基础设施。这是一个挑战。这是我们几乎每天都会谈论的话题。

paras.en: Kobalt announced a $700 million fund in 2023 to buy music catalogs. Is that part of this deal, or do you retain that at Kobalt?
paras.zh: Kobalt 宣布将于 2023 年拨款 7 亿美元用于购买音乐目录。这是这笔交易的一部分吗？或者你会在 Kobalt 保留它吗？

paras.en: Hubert: We retain [it], and that’s a conversation that I had [with Larry] because we have a different IP strategy and we deploy on different type of copyrights. For us, the idea here was to provide an additional service to our clients, and we provided all the services under a lending situation. But if people needed a capital event, we wanted to be able to say yes, we can do that for you as well. We created a fund in ’11 and a second fund in ’16. We created that fund in 2023, and we’ve been deploying the capital, obviously, not only on clients that we have because we know them and they come to us, but we’re also buying third-party copyrights.
paras.zh: 休伯特：我们保留[它]，这是我[与拉里]的一次谈话，因为我们有不同的知识产权战略，并且我们部署了不同类型的版权。对于我们来说，这里的想法是为我们的客户提供额外的服务，并且我们在贷款情况下提供了所有服务。但如果人们需要一场资本活动，我们希望能够答应，我们也可以为您做到这一点。我们在 11 年创建了一只基金，在 16 年创建了第二只基金。我们于 2023 年创建了该基金，显然，我们一直在部署资金，不仅是因为我们了解他们并且他们来找我们，而且我们还购买第三方版权。

paras.en: Mestel: We turn down many more deals than we do, and so Laurent’s team is participating in our deal meetings. When there’s a deal that we’re reviewing that isn’t right for Primary Wave, we’re turning it over to Kobalt [now].
paras.zh: 梅斯特：我们拒绝的交易比我们拒绝的交易多得多，因此 Laurent 的团队正在参加我们的交易会议。当我们正在审查的交易不适合 Primary Wave 时，我们[现在]会将其移交给 Kobalt。

paras.en: Larry, I think one of the most interesting things Primary Wave has done from a marketing perspective is the Whitney Houston slot machines in Las Vegas. How are those going? Are they a success?
paras.zh: 拉里，我认为从营销角度来看，Primary Wave 所做的最有趣的事情之一是拉斯维加斯的惠特尼·休斯顿老虎机。那些进展如何？他们成功了吗？

paras.en: Mestel: It has been a giant success for us. We started this in 2024, and we budgeted 200 machines a year. Now, we’ve done over 500 a year. We just renewed the deal with [slot machine manufacturer] IGT. We are having great success, but how do you measure success? Well, you can measure success on shipping machines and shipping more than your budget, but the real measure is that we’re making more money for the estate of Whitney Houston, which we own 50% of, [on slot machines] than the entire estate was generating six and a half years ago when we bought into the estate on that one deal.
paras.zh: 梅斯特尔：这对我们来说是一个巨大的成功。我们于 2024 年开始这项工作，每年预算 200 台机器。现在，我们每年已经完成了 500 多个。我们刚刚与[老虎机制造商] IGT 续签了协议。我们取得了巨大的成功，但是你如何衡量成功呢？好吧，你可以用运输机来衡量成功与否，运输量是否超出了你的预算，但真正的衡量标准是，我们为惠特尼·休斯顿（Whitney Houston）庄园（我们拥有该庄园 50% 的股份）[通过老虎机]赚到的钱比六年半前我们通过一笔交易购买该庄园时整个庄园的收入还要多。

paras.en: Larry, you often talk about how you guys partner with the estates when you do these deals, but I know estates can be really sensitive about certain brand partnerships. Like, anything that involves sex, alcohol or even gambling. What was that conversation like with the Houston estate to decide that this was right for her legacy?
paras.zh: 拉里，你经常谈论在进行这些交易时如何与庄园合作，但我知道庄园对某些品牌合作伙伴关系可能非常敏感。比如，任何涉及性、酒精甚至赌博的事情。与休斯顿遗产委员会的谈话如何决定这是否适合她的遗产？

paras.en: Mestel: It was easy. Whitney loved to play slot machines. It was very organic. We will not do a brand deal, a marketing deal, any type of brand alliance, movie, anything unless the artist estate 100% signs off and says yes.
paras.zh: 梅斯特尔：这很容易。惠特尼喜欢玩老虎机。这是非常有机的。我们不会做品牌交易、营销交易、任何类型的品牌联盟、电影、任何事情，除非艺术家财产 100% 签字同意。

paras.en: Willard Ahdritz, founder of Kobalt, is stepping away from his role as chairman as part of this deal. Who is now filling that role?
paras.zh: 作为此次交易的一部分，Kobalt 创始人威拉德·阿德里茨 (Willard Ahdritz) 将辞去董事长职务。现在谁来填补这个角色？

paras.en: Mestel: The reality is there’s only one person that matters, which is the CEO, which is Laurent. We were clear with each other day one that the reason why Primary Wave was doing this, a big chunk of the reason, was the management team in Laurent and Kobalt. It is an entrepreneurial company. Laurent runs it with very little interference at all from Primary Wave. We talk a couple times a week, so we’re very active on what we’re doing together. Kobalt is and will remain a separate entrepreneurially-run company.
paras.zh: 梅斯特尔：现实情况是，只有一个人是重要的，那就是首席执行官，也就是劳伦特。第一天我们就彼此明确，Primary Wave 这样做的原因，很大一部分原因是 Laurent 和 Kobalt 的管理团队。这是一家创业公司。 Laurent 运行它时几乎没有受到 Primary Wave 的干扰。我们每周聊几次，所以我们对一起做的事情非常积极。 Kobalt 现在并将继续是一家独立的创业公司。

paras.en: Both Primary Wave and Kobalt have active funds to buy more catalogs. Kobalt’s is a $700 million fund, announced in 2023 with Morgan Stanley, and Primary Wave’s is a $2.2 billion fund with Brookfield, announced in the spring. How much of these funds have you both deployed so far?
paras.zh: Primary Wave 和 Kobalt 都有积极的资金来购买更多目录。 Kobalt’s 是与摩根士丹利 (Morgan Stanley) 于 2023 年共同推出的 7 亿美元基金，Primary Wave’s 是与 Brookfield 共同推出的 22 亿美元基金，于今年春季宣布。到目前为止，你们已经部署了多少资金？

paras.en: Mestel: We are way ahead of schedule. We’ve deployed almost 60% of our most current fund, which we only closed back in April of this year. There have been some very, very large-scale deals, and our pipeline is pretty significant. So we anticipate being probably 75% invested at the end of the year and fully invested the first quarter of next year. We have many pools of capital. We have a permanent evergreen fund with Brookfield. Brookfield put $2 billion on [the] primary balance sheet four and a half years ago, whenever that was, 2022, and we have a lot of surprises.
paras.zh: 梅斯特尔：我们比计划提前了很多。我们已经部署了近 60% 的最新基金，该基金于今年 4 月才关闭。已经发生了一些非常非常大规模的交易，我们的管道非常重要。因此，我们预计年底可能会完成 75% 的投资，并在明年第一季度完成全部投资。我们有很多资金池。我们与布鲁克菲尔德有一个永久的常青基金。四年前，无论是 2022 年，布鲁克菲尔德在主要资产负债表上投入了 20 亿美元，我们有很多惊喜。

paras.en: Hubert: We’ve deployed about half a billion dollars of the $700 million, and we intend to spend the [remainder] of that $200 million going forward. So there will be a new fund [soon] … [Primary Wave and Kobalt] don’t go after the same targets at all. We typically buy more recent vintages. We buy copyrights where we have high incentives of digital royalties because we want to take advantage of the AMRA capabilities.
paras.zh: 休伯特：我们已经部署了 7 亿美元中的大约 5 亿美元，我们打算继续使用这 2 亿美元的[剩余]。所以[很快]就会有一只新基金……[Primary Wave 和 Kobalt] 根本不追求相同的目标。我们通常会购买较新的年份。我们购买具有高数字版权费激励的版权，因为我们希望利用 AMRA 功能。

paras.en: 2026 has been a year full of major music business acquisitions. UMG’s Virgin Music Group acquired Downtown, BMG bought Concord and Primary Wave acquired Kobalt. On a macro scale, why do you think these acquisitions and this consolidation is happening now?
paras.zh: 2026 年是音乐业务发生重大收购的一年。 UMG 的 Virgin Music Group 收购了 Downtown，BMG 收购了 Concord，Primary Wave 收购了 Kobalt。从宏观层面来看，您认为为什么现在会发生这些收购和整合？

paras.en: Mestel: I think you can see a lot more. I think as interest rates go up, I think you will see a lot of our competitors that are financially driven looking to sell. Primary Wave, by the way, has no debt, so we’re generating significant returns without that because of the alpha we’re creating as we market. A lot of our competitors are highly leveraged, so they’re taking very safe assets that generate cash flow every single day that would normally go back out into acquisition, or go back out in the form of dividends to investors. These companies are paying interest to banks, and as interest rates go up and they have to refinance their significant debt, they’re going to have a hard time. I don’t name competitors, but you’re going to see a lot of people that are going to be selling, I think, over the course of the next two and three years. So you’ll see a lot more consolidation, and that’s great for companies like Kobalt and Primary Wave, especially ones that are very well capitalized and have almost no debt.
paras.zh: 梅斯特尔：我认为你可以看到更多。我认为随着利率上升，你会看到我们的许多竞争对手在经济上寻求出售。顺便说一句，Primary Wave 没有债务，因此，由于我们在营销时创造了阿尔法，因此即使没有债务，我们也能产生可观的回报。我们的许多竞争对手的杠杆率很高，因此他们正在获取非常安全的资产，这些资产每天都会产生现金流，这些现金流通常会重新用于收购，或以向投资者分红的形式返回。这些公司向银行支付利息，随着利率上升，他们必须为巨额债务再融资，他们的日子将会很艰难。我没有透露竞争对手的名字，但我认为，在未来两三年内，你会看到很多人将出售产品。所以你会看到更多的整合，这对于像 Kobalt 和 Primary Wave 这样的公司来说是件好事，尤其是那些资本充足且几乎没有债务的公司。

paras.en: But is it better for artists and songwriters?
paras.zh: 但这对艺术家和词曲作者来说更好吗？

paras.en: Mestel: Well, it’s better if you’re with a company that has an infrastructure to create content for them and to actually market [their music]. Is it any good when an artist is acquired by a private equity firm? Probably not, because the first thing on their mind isn’t legacy protection, and it’s not turning a hit song that was a hit 30 years ago into a hit song again. It’s, how are they going to extract as much cash out of the asset as they possibly can, and then likely flip it? So yeah, I think it’s very good if the artist is being acquired by a company that has the ability to do something.
paras.zh: 梅斯特尔：嗯，如果你所在的公司拥有为他们创建内容并实际营销[他们的音乐]的基础设施，那就更好了。艺术家被私募股权公司收购有什么好处吗？可能不会，因为他们首先想到的不是遗产保护，也不是把30年前的热门歌曲再次变成热门歌曲。问题是，他们如何从资产中提取尽可能多的现金，然后可能将其翻转？所以，是的，我认为如果艺术家被一家有能力做某事的公司收购，那是非常好的。

articles.title: FX Gives Gen Z Comedy ‘Adults’ Third Season Renewal
articles.author: Etan Vlessing

paras.en: The Gen Z comedy Adults has got a third season order from FX.
paras.zh: Z 世代喜剧《成人》已获得 FX 的第三季订单。

paras.en: The 16-episode order for FXX and Hulu has also earned creators Ben Kronengold and Rebecca Shaw a new overall deal with FX Productions. “Ben and Rebecca have elevated Adults in every way, earning critical praise and a legion of devoted fans who have embraced the friend group as their own,” FX Entertainment president Nick Grad said in a statement.
paras.zh: FXX 和 Hulu 的 16 集订单也为创作者 Ben Kronengold 和 Rebecca Shaw 赢得了与 FX Productions 的新整体协议。 FX Entertainment 总裁尼克·格莱德 (Nick Grad) 在一份声明中表示：“本和丽贝卡在各个方面都提升了《成人》的水平，赢得了广泛的赞誉和大批忠实粉丝，他们将这个朋友团体视为自己的团体。”

paras.en: “Adults showed significant growth in its sophomore year and we’ve seen the show inspire everything from memes to Halloween costumes, so the decision was easy — more episodes and a new deal at FX for Ben and Rebecca!” he added. Adults stars Malik Elassal, Lucy Freyer, Jack Innanen, Amita Rao and Owen Thiele as five friends sharing a house in Queens and few boundaries.
paras.zh: “成人节目在第二年就表现出了显着的增长，我们已经看到该节目激发了从表情包到万圣节服装的一切灵感，所以决定很简单——更多剧集以及 FX 为 Ben 和 Rebecca 提供的新优惠！”他补充道。在《成人》中，马利克·埃拉萨尔、露西·弗雷尔、杰克·伊纳宁、阿米塔·拉奥和欧文·蒂勒饰演五个朋友，他们在皇后区合租一所房子，几乎没有界限。

paras.en: “We started working with FX over six years ago, back when Paul Baker was but a twinkle in all of our eyes,” Kronengold and Shaw said in their own statement. “In the years since, John and the rest of the team have taught us everything we know about how to lead, produce, and tell stories that make people feel like part of a community. They’ve become family, and we’re so glad to make it official — and to start yelling at them like we do our parents.”
paras.zh: Kronengold 和 Shaw 在自己的声明中表示：“我们六年多前就开始与 FX 合作，当时 Paul Baker 还只是我们眼中的闪光点。” “从那以后的几年里，约翰和团队的其他成员教会了我们所有关于如何领导、制作和讲述故事的知识，让人们感觉自己是社区的一部分。他们已经成为一家人，我们很高兴正式宣布这一点——并开始像我们的父母一样对他们大喊大叫。”

paras.en: The second season saw streaming viewership doubling after the release of the standalone prequel episode Marathon Day, FX said. Season two of Adults was executive produced by Kronengold, Shaw, Nick Kroll, Sarah Naftalis, Jonathan Krisel, Alicia Van Couvering and Rob Rosell.
